newsitem.title: JAPAN: Top aide to North Korea's Kim Jong-il in Japan.
newsitem.headline: Top aide to North Korea's Kim Jong-il in Japan.

text.p: A North Korea delegation led by a top aide to de facto leader Kim Jong-il arrived in Japan on Thursday for a 13-day visit to promote "scholarly exchanges".

The four-member delegation headed by Hwang Jang-yop, secretary of the ruling Workers' (Communist) Party, will attend an international seminar in Tokyo on how countries can adapt to the 21st century, organisers said.
Experts on North Korea in Japan consider Hwang a close adviser to Kim Jong-il.
"Their visit will constitute nothing political," said a source close to the North Korean government, who asked not to be identified.
Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto told South Korean President Kim Young-sam at a weekend meeting that Japanese government officials would not meet the North Koreans.
About 20 North Korean scholars will arrive in Japan early next month to join the delegation and attend the seminar, the source said.
Japan, which has a large ethnic Korean population, has diplomatic ties with South Korea, but not with North Korea.
